advancements.survivalreimagined.emi_info: Check EMI for infos on blocks and items

Many blocks and items work differently in this pack. Hover over one in your inventory or in EMI's list and press R (or left click) for its recipes or U (or right click) for its uses: the Info tab explains what it does
advancements.survivalreimagined.framing_: Craft a Framing Table to customize the look of your Storage Drawers
advancements.survivalreimagined.atlas.de: Craft an Atlas. Add Paper or Empty Maps to it to draw new maps as you explore
advancements.survivalreimagined.heartsto: Craft a pair of Heartstones and give the second one to a friend
advancements.survivalreimagined.capture_: Craft a Capture Net to catch small critters like Butterflies, Snails and Bees
advancements.survivalreimagined.catch_bu: Catch a Butterfly with a Capture Net in forests or plains. Butterflies pollinate flowers and help crops grow
advancements.survivalreimagined.froglass: Let a Frog eat a Dragonfly, found in swamps, to get Froglass, a colored glass block
Craft a Whistle to make your pets follow you or wander freely
advancements.survivalreimagined.knapsack: Craft a Knapsack from Hide, dropped by Boars, Rhinos, Elephants and Komodo Dragons, to carry a baby animal and release it elsewhere
advancements.survivalreimagined.shellsto: Snails drop Snail Shells: craft them with Calcite into Shellstone, a decorative stone
advancements.survivalreimagined.glow_goo: Cook Glow Berries in a Smoker or on a Campfire, or kill a Firefly, to get Glow Goop. Place it for light or turn it into Spectral Arrows at a Fletching Table
advancements.survivalreimagined.cooked_m: Mammoths in snowy biomes drop Mammoth Meat: cook and eat it for a meal as filling as a Steak
advancements.survivalreimagined.crab_cla: Coconuts can release a Coconut Crab when they break. Its Claw works as Shears and gives +1 reach when held
advancements.survivalreimagined.tropical: Eat a Tropical Stew, a very filling meal made from a Coconut Slice and Cooked Crab Meat
advancements.survivalreimagined.coconut_: Break a Coconut with an Axe for Coconut Slices. Eating one clears all effects and leaves a Husk, usable as a Bowl
advancements.survivalreimagined.exotic_s: Craft Coconut or Walnut Leaves with Shears to get a sapling. Coconut trees grow on beaches, Walnut trees in plains
advancements.survivalreimagined.seashell: Collect Seashells on beaches and craft them into Seashell Tiles, a decorative block
advancements.survivalreimagined.prickly_: Prickly Pears grow on fully grown Cacti. They cure Wither, but eating them raw hurts: cook them first
emi.info.supplementaries.wind_vane.1: Spins with the weather and emits a redstone signal: weak when raining, stronger when thundering, and briefly when hit by a Wind Charge.
emi.info.supplementaries.wind_vane.2: Also strongly powers the block below it, so it works well on rooftops.
emi.info.supplementaries.cog_block: A solid block that carries redstone like dust: power one and it powers the Cog Blocks next to it, losing strength along the way. Great for compact vertical wiring.
emi.info.supplementaries.crystal_display: Shows a number or symbol based on the redstone signal strength it receives. Displays placed side by side can be chained to show bigger numbers.
emi.info.supplementaries.relayer.1: Copies the signal in front of it to its back, with a tiny delay. Works with indirect power from redstone dust too.
emi.info.supplementaries.relayer.2: Carries analog signals without loss, and chains of Relayers can sit next to each other without interfering: ideal for arrays of Crystal Displays.
emi.info.supplementaries.grouper.1: Compares the blocks on its two sides and outputs from its back: a full signal if they are identical (state included), a weaker one if they are the same block in a different state (e.g. crops at different ages).
emi.info.supplementaries.grouper.2: If neither side has a full face towards it, it compares entities instead: the same type gives a weaker signal, the same item, variant, color, profession or name gives a full one.
emi.info.supplementaries.spring_launcher: Extends like a piston when powered, launching entities on top of it much farther than a piston and slime block. It can't push blocks.
Falling on an extended one from high enough bounces you up, and standing on it lets you jump slightly higher.
emi.info.supplementaries.speaker_block.1: When powered, sends a message in chat (or through the narrator) to players within its radius. Edit the message and volume from its GUI.
emi.info.supplementaries.speaker_block.2: Rename it in an Anvil to change the name shown in chat.
emi.info.supplementaries.turn_table.1: When powered, rotates the block it faces: the stronger the signal, the faster it rotates. A short pulse rotates it once.
emi.info.supplementaries.turn_table.2: Right-click to reverse the direction. Facing up, it also spins entities standing on it, and rotating a container shuffles its content.
emi.info.supplementaries.turn_table.3: Turns Pulleys connected to its axis.
emi.info.supplementaries.pulley_block.1: Holds Ropes or Chains in its single slot. When rotated by a Turn Table or a Crank, it unwinds them or winds them back up depending on the direction, carrying the block attached at the end.
emi.info.supplementaries.pulley_block.2: Rotates adjacent Pulleys on the same axis, and nearby chained Pulleys can pass ropes to each other, even horizontally.
emi.info.supplementaries.clock_block.1: Shows the current in-game time; right-click it to read the time. A Comparator reads the time of day, and it gives an observer update every in-game hour.
emi.info.supplementaries.clock_block.2: Unlike Daylight Detectors it isn't fooled by rain, but it doesn't work in the Nether or the End.
emi.info.supplementaries.dispenser_minec: A Minecart carrying a Dispenser that fires its content while it rides on a powered Activator Rail.
emi.info.supplementaries.bellows.1: When powered, blows air in front of it at a speed based on the signal: pushes entities, speeds up furnaces next to it, keeps nearby fire alive and speeds up copper oxidation.
emi.info.supplementaries.bellows.2: Compresses when stepped on. Blowing on a wet Sponge touching a Soap Block makes bubbles.
emi.info.supplementaries.redstone_illumi: A light that is on by default and gets dimmer the stronger the redstone signal it receives.
emi.info.supplementaries.crank: An analog lever: each turn changes its redstone signal. Right-click to turn it clockwise, sneak right-click for counterclockwise. Can also turn Pulleys.
emi.info.supplementaries.faucet.1: Right-click its handle to open or close it; a redstone signal inverts its state.
emi.info.supplementaries.faucet.2: Open, it drops items from the inventory below one at a time, or pours fluids from the block behind it (cauldrons, jars, waterlogged blocks, beehives...) into the container below, a bit at a time.
emi.info.supplementaries.faucet.3: It can also wet concrete powder, turn dirt into mud and void fluids into sponges.
emi.info.supplementaries.hourglass.1: Fill it with sand, dust, powder, slime or honey: the content slowly falls, with a duration based on the material, and a Comparator reads the remaining time.
emi.info.supplementaries.hourglass.2: Reset it by sneak right-clicking or by rotating it twice with a Turn Table.
emi.info.supplementaries.lock_block: Can be locked with a Key. Emits a redstone pulse when a player with the correct Key interacts with it.
emi.info.supplementaries.sconce_lever: A Sconce that works as a Lever. When unlit, its behaviour is inverted.
emi.info.supplementaries.cannon.1: Shoots any item: blocks are placed where they land and projectiles are fired as entities. The more power, the more Gunpowder each shot uses. Fire it with Flint and Steel, a gunpowder trail or redstone.
emi.info.supplementaries.cannon.2: Sneak right-click (or the maneuver button) to aim: move the mouse to aim, scroll to change power, Space to switch aiming mode, left-click to fire, E or Sneak to exit. The trajectory shows where the shot will land.
emi.info.supplementaries.cannon.3: Shooting a Void Pearl teleports you. With no ammo, sneak right-click its muzzle with an empty hand to climb inside.
emi.info.supplementaries.cannonball.1: Cannon ammo that breaks blocks based on its kinetic energy, slowing down with each block depending on its hardness. Bounces off the ground at steep angles and transfers energy to entities it hits.
emi.info.supplementaries.cannonball.2: Killing a Creeper in one hit with a Cannonball makes it drop a music disc.
emi.info.supplementaries.enderman_head: When worn, gives you the vision you'd get spectating a Voidman. Placed, it opens its mouth and emits a redstone signal while you stare at it, stronger the longer you look.
Brighter than candles. Place on floors, walls or ceilings and stack them to make candelabras and chandeliers.
Light them with Flint and Steel, Fire Charges, flaming arrows or gunpowder trails; put them out with a Shovel or water.
emi.info.supplementaries.sconces: Decorative alternatives to torches. Light them with Flint and Steel, Fire Charges, flaming arrows or gunpowder trails; water or a Splash Water Bottle puts them out without breaking them.
emi.info.supplementaries.awnings.1: Right-click with an empty hand to tilt it. Falling on one makes you bounce off depending on its angle, and sneaking on it lets you fall through.
emi.info.supplementaries.awnings.2: Can be placed on the top or bottom half of a block, against supporting blocks or other Awnings.
emi.info.supplementaries.pedestal.1: Displays one item on top; swords, tools and tridents get special poses. Stacked Pedestals connect visually.
emi.info.supplementaries.pedestal.2: Taking or placing an item gives an observer update, useful for traps.
emi.info.supplementaries.flags.1: Horizontal banners that wave in the wind, with their own set of pattern textures. Crafted from Banners.
emi.info.supplementaries.flags.2: Placed on top of a pole of placed Sticks, they can be raised and lowered.
emi.info.supplementaries.buntings: Colorful decorations that sway in the wind. Place them on Ropes, walls or ceilings.
emi.info.supplementaries.presents: Holds one item stack. From its GUI you can address it to a player and add a short description: once packed, only you and the recipient can open it.
emi.info.supplementaries.pignata.1: Hangs when placed under a block and can be tied to a Lead. Right-click with items to stuff it (hoppers work too).
emi.info.supplementaries.pignata.2: Bursts after taking enough damage (fall damage included), dropping its content. Slowly heals over time.
emi.info.supplementaries.slidy_block: Right-click to push it. It keeps sliding on ice and changes direction randomly on Soap Blocks.
emi.info.supplementaries.soap_block: Entities walking on it slip. A Bellows blowing on a wet Sponge touching it makes bubbles.
emi.info.supplementaries.sugar_cube: Dissolves when it touches water or rain. Feeding it to a horse gives it a short speed boost.
emi.info.supplementaries.gravel_bricks: Breaks when jumped or fallen on. The Suspicious variant can hide an item, like Suspicious Gravel.
emi.info.supplementaries.notice_board: Displays a Written Book, a Map or a Banner Pattern. Books show one page at a time, and a redstone pulse turns the page. Wax it to prevent interactions.
emi.info.supplementaries.fodder: Hungry farm animals eat its layers: babies grow faster and adults go into love mode (with the usual cooldown). Can be placed by Dispensers; use a Hoe to remove a layer.
emi.info.supplementaries.bamboo_spikes.1: Slow down and damage mobs walking through them.
emi.info.supplementaries.bamboo_spikes.2: Infuse them with a harmful Lingering Potion by crafting, clicking on them or pouring it with a Faucet to apply its effect too.
emi.info.supplementaries.hat_stand: Like an Armor Stand, but only holds a helmet. Sneak right-click with an empty hand to wobble it.
emi.info.supplementaries.lumisene.1: A finite, glowing liquid made of layers: it spreads out as thin as possible and floats on water. A Bucket picks up or places a full block's worth of connected layers.
emi.info.supplementaries.lumisene.2: Sets on fire instantly across all connected blocks. Walking through it gives Flammable (fire lasts longer and you spread it as you walk); drinking a bottle gives Glowing and Flammable.
emi.info.supplementaries.planter: Grows any plant or crop without water, even in the Nether, and crops on it can't be trampled.
emi.info.supplementaries.blackboard.1: Draw black and white pictures on it from its GUI, or directly by clicking with a dye (not consumed). Accepts Glow Ink.
emi.info.supplementaries.blackboard.2: Keeps its drawing when broken and can be copied like Banners. Clean it with a wet Sponge or Soap; wax it to prevent interactions.
emi.info.supplementaries.timber_frames: Frames, Braces and Cross Braces can hold any solid block: click a placed one with the block. An Axe breaks the frame and leaves the block.
emi.info.supplementaries.ash.1: Fire leaves Ash on the blocks it burns, but most logs turn into Burnt Logs instead: break them to get Ash. Mobs that die while burning also drop Ash.
emi.info.supplementaries.ash.2: Placed Ash falls like sand and rain slowly washes it away. Ash layers also cover the Basalt in Basalt Deltas.
emi.info.supplementaries.daub: A medieval building block: placed inside a Timber Frame, Brace or Cross Brace, it becomes Wattle and Daub.
emi.info.supplementaries.netherite_doors: Can be locked with a Key: once locked, only players with the correct Key can open them. Anyone can use them until they are locked.
emi.info.supplementaries.gold_doors: While powered by redstone, they can't be opened or closed by hand.
emi.info.supplementaries.iron_gate: A sturdier Fence Gate that connects visually to the gates above and below it.
emi.info.supplementaries.rope.1: Place it under a ceiling, on fences or walls or next to other Ropes; like Scaffolding, it only reaches so far horizontally. Vertical Ropes are climbable and stop fall damage; horizontal ones can be walked on, slowly.
emi.info.supplementaries.rope.2: Place a Rope against a vertical one to extend it down, pushing the block at its end; sneak right-click with an empty hand to pull it up, lifting that block (great for wells). Shears remove the bottom connection.
emi.info.supplementaries.rope.3: Burns quickly and breaks when hit by projectiles, along with the Ropes it supports.
emi.info.supplementaries.flint_block: Pushed by a Piston against an iron-like block (or vice versa), it makes sparks that set nearby flammable blocks on fire. Walking on it with Iron Boots does the same.
emi.info.supplementaries.feather_block: Extremely fluffy: you sink slowly into it and take no fall damage.
emi.info.supplementaries.doormat: Holds a few lines of text, and cats like to sit on it. Sneak right-click one of its sides to hide an item under it.
emi.info.supplementaries.way_signs.1: Up to two can be placed on a fence or placed Stick, or against a wall. They point where you face when placing them; sneak right-click to flip one.
emi.info.supplementaries.way_signs.2: Click it with a Compass to point it towards the Compass target. Can be dyed like signs.
emi.info.supplementaries.flower_box: Holds flowers and plants, including tall ones and vines. Can be placed on the side or middle of a block, or hanging from a ceiling.
emi.info.supplementaries.statue: Holds an item in its hand; candles, tools and swords have special poses. Waves when powered by redstone.
emi.info.supplementaries.goblet: Holds and displays a drink: potions, honey, milk, soups and more. Right-click to drink it instantly. Readable by Comparators.
emi.info.supplementaries.jar.1: Holds cookie-like foods, which you can eat straight from it, or bottles of a liquid like a Goblet.
emi.info.supplementaries.jar.2: It can also capture small creatures: click one with the Jar.
emi.info.supplementaries.slingshot: Shoots blocks, which place themselves where they land when possible. Can be enchanted with Quick Charge and Multishot.
emi.info.supplementaries.quiver.1: Holds several stacks of different arrows; add them by clicking a stack onto it like a Bundle. Arrows you pick up go inside if it has room for them.
emi.info.supplementaries.quiver.2: Use it to pick the arrow to shoot (with the mouse, arrow keys, number keys or the scroll wheel) without slowing down, or sneak right-click to cycle.
emi.info.supplementaries.quiver.3: Some Skeletons carry one and can drop it.
emi.info.supplementaries.confetti_popper: Makes confetti! Can be worn as a party hat (Creepers can wear them too). Sneak to place a layer on the ground.
emi.info.supplementaries.cannon_boats: A Boat with a Cannon. Press Ctrl to fire while driving, or Space to enter maneuver mode.
emi.info.supplementaries.altimeter: Its texture shows your height and changes with the dimension. Right-click to see your Y level.
emi.info.supplementaries.slice_map: A Map showing the world as seen at the Y level where it was created, with a smaller range. You need to be at that level to map it, so it can't be used as X-ray.
emi.info.supplementaries.flute.1: Click a pet or horse to bind it to the Flute, then play it to call nearby bound pets that aren't sitting.
emi.info.supplementaries.flute.2: Plays a random song; rename it to a song's name to always play that one.
emi.info.supplementaries.wrench.1: Rotates nearly any block, including signs, chests and beds, around the axis of the clicked face; sneak right-click to reverse. Left-click to rotate Item Frames and Armor Stands.
emi.info.supplementaries.wrench.2: Also a fast melee weapon, as strong as a Wooden Sword.
emi.info.supplementaries.bombs.1: Thrown projectiles that explode where they land, damaging mobs while only breaking weak blocks like grass. They can ignite nearby Creepers.
emi.info.supplementaries.bombs.2: Blue Bombs, found while exploring, flash before going off, then deal heavy area damage, set entities on fire and inflict Weakness.
emi.info.supplementaries.rope_arrow.1: Deploys a coil of Ropes where it lands, great for exploring caves. Holds a limited number of Ropes: craft it in the Fletching Table and refill it with Ropes in the crafting grid.
emi.info.supplementaries.rope_arrow.2: Ropes it didn't place stay in the arrow, so pick it back up.
emi.info.supplementaries.antique_ink: Found in Urns and fishing. Use it on a sign to give it an antique font; craft it with a Map for an Antique Map, or with a Written Book for a Tattered Book that can't be copied.
emi.info.supplementaries.key.1: Rename it in an Anvil to set a password, then click a Netherite Door, Netherite Trapdoor or Lock Block to lock it. Sneak right-click with the correct Key to unlock it.
emi.info.supplementaries.key.2: To open a locked block the Key only needs to be in your inventory. Dispensers can use it too.
emi.info.supplementaries.candy: A sweet that is very quick to eat. Eating too many at once has side effects.
emi.info.supplementaries.pancake.1: Like cakes, eaten once placed. Stack them in a pile and top them with Honey (by clicking or with a Faucet) for a short Speed boost when eaten.
emi.info.supplementaries.pancake.2: Put one in a Jukebox for some sick tunes!
emi.info.supplementaries.music_discs: Pancake: play a Pancake in a Jukebox. Heave Ho: kill a Creeper in one hit with a Cannonball.
emi.info.supplementaries.flax: A tall crop used for Ropes, Fodder, Doormats and more.
emi.info.supplementaries.urn: Found in small patches deep underground. Breaking one drops loot, usually bones or ores but rarely something great like bombs or enchanted gear. Fortune improves the loot.
emi.info.supplementaries.placeable_gunpo: Gunpowder can be placed on the ground as a trail. Light it with fire, Fire Charges, flaming arrows or lava: it burns along the trail and ignites TNT, flammable blocks, campfires and candles.
emi.info.supplementaries.throwable_brick: Bricks can be thrown at your foes, and break glass blocks they hit.
emi.info.supplementaries.soap.1: Craft it with dyed items to remove their color, or use it on dyed blocks, armor, pets, Sheep and Slimes to wash them.
emi.info.supplementaries.soap.2: Removes wax and oxidation from copper in one use, and cleans Blackboards, Maps, Sticky Pistons, tipped Bamboo Spikes and more. Also washes away the Slimed effect.
emi.info.supplementaries.bubble_blower: Blows soap bubbles at your friends. Recharge it by crafting it with Soap.
emi.info.supplementaries.throwable_slime: Slimeballs can be thrown and bounce off anything. Hit entities get the Slimed effect, which lowers their jump height until it wears off or is washed away with water or Soap. Slimes can apply it too.
emi.info.supplementaries.placeable_stick: Sticks and Blaze Rods can be placed on the ground, a few per block. Placed Blaze Rods burn entities standing on them and bubble underwater.
emi.info.supplementaries.raked_gravel: Use a Hoe on Gravel to rake it in the direction you are facing. It can go in any direction and curve.
emi.info.supplementaries.placeable_books: Books can be placed on the ground: normal books stand side by side with random colors, enchanted ones are piled up.
emi.info.supplementaries.item_lore: Craft a renamed Name Tag with any item to add its name as lore to the item.
emi.info.supplementaries.clock: Shows the time of day from the position of the sun and moon, even underground. Right-click it to see the exact time. Doesn't work in the Nether or the End.
emi.info.supplementaries.blast_armor_tri: Rarely caught as treasure while fishing.
emi.info.supplementaries.cartographers_q: Treasure and explorer maps found in chests come as a Cartographer's Quill instead. Keep it in your inventory: after a while it finishes drawing and turns into the map. If it finds nothing nearby, try again somewhere else.
emi.info.supplementaries.spider_head: Dropped by Spiders killed by a Charged Creeper's explosion, like the other mob heads.
emi.info.supplementaries.enderman_head.s: Dropped by Endermen killed by a Charged Creeper's explosion.
emi.info.amendments.lanterns: Lanterns can be placed on walls, where they swing when hit by entities. Lanterns hanging from a ceiling fall if their support is broken.
emi.info.amendments.cauldron.1: Cauldrons can hold any liquid. Click one with an item to craft it with the liquid inside, or throw the ingredients in.
emi.info.amendments.cauldron.2: Mix potions in it, or dye its water with dyes (dyed water can be mixed too) and fill Dye Bottles from it.
emi.info.amendments.cauldron.3: With a heat source below, water and potions boil and hurt whoever stands in them. A boiling water cauldron can cook stews from the ingredients thrown in. Walking into a splash or lingering potion applies it.
emi.info.amendments.dye_bottle: Dyed water taken from a Cauldron. Pour it into a Cauldron to dye its water.
emi.info.amendments.lectern: Placing a Book and Quill on it opens a writing screen with a Quill button to change font and an Ink Well button to change text color. Works with Hoppers.
emi.info.amendments.hanging_signs: Hanging Signs can hold an item (or a Banner Pattern) on each face. Attached to walls they swing, and they connect visually to fences and walls.
emi.info.amendments.carpets: Carpets can be placed on Slabs and Stairs.
emi.info.amendments.mob_heads: Mob heads can be stacked on top of each other in any combination, and you can place one or more Candles on them.
emi.info.amendments.lily_pad: Any block can be placed on a Lily Pad: it becomes a waterlogged block with the Lily Pad on top, and goes back to normal when removed.
emi.info.amendments.bell: Ring a Bell by interacting with the Chains or Ropes hanging below it, even long ones.
emi.info.amendments.ceiling_decor: Banners and Flower Pots can be placed on ceilings.
emi.info.amendments.tripwire_hook: Sneak right-click a placed Tripwire Hook with a tool to hang it there.
emi.info.amendments.fire_charge.1: Fire Charges can be thrown and are affected by gravity. They set things on fire where they land.
emi.info.amendments.fire_charge.2: Dragon Charges are a Dragon's Breath version that leaves a lingering cloud. Dispensers shoot both.
emi.info.amendments.torch: Hitting a mob with a Torch in your main hand sets it on fire for a moment.
emi.info.amendments.jukebox: Jukeboxes show the disc they are playing, which spins while the music plays.
emi.info.clayworks.kiln: A furnace for building materials: it bakes Bricks, Terracotta, Glass, smooth and cracked stones and similar blocks faster than a Furnace, using the same fuels.
emi.info.clayworks.pottery_table: Used to customize Decorated Pots: change their color with a Dye, or add a trim by choosing a pattern and a trim material (Iron, Copper, Gold, Lapis, Amethyst, Diamond, Emerald, Netherite...).
emi.info.boatload.furnace_boat: A boat with a Furnace that burns fuel to go faster. Sneak right-click it to open the fuel slot. The Furnace takes a seat, so it carries only one passenger.
emi.info.boatload.large_boat: A wider boat that carries more passengers, or fewer if some of them are large mobs.
emi.info.bitsandbalance.glow_goo.1: Throw it to leave a bright Glow Goo Splatter where it lands, which works as a light source even underwater. Mobs and players hit by it glow for a while.
emi.info.bitsandbalance.glow_goo.2: Brewed into a Potion of Glowing (made from Glow Berries), it gives a Potion of Bioluminescence, which makes you emit light.
emi.info.bitsandbalance.music_disc_dog: Dropped by Creepers killed by a Skeleton, like the other Music Discs, and found in some chests.
emi.info.bitsandbalance.tipped_arrow: When it lands, a Tipped Arrow leaves a lingering cloud of its effect and becomes a normal arrow. Arrows shot by mobs, like Strays and Bogged, do the same.
emi.info.hangglider.hang_glider: Right-click to open it, then jump from a high place to glide. Sneak to dive faster. It loses durability quickly while gliding and is repaired with Phantom Membranes in an Anvil.
emi.info.sawmill.sawmill: A Stonecutter for wood: put in Logs or Planks and choose any wooden item to make it directly, often for fewer planks than the crafting recipe.
emi.info.labels.label.1: Like an Item Frame, but it fits on any surface and lets you open the block behind it, perfect for chests and storage.
emi.info.labels.label.2: Sneak right-click it with an item to show that item. Dye it to change its color, use a Glow Ink Sac to make it glow, or a Feather to show the item's name.
emi.info.strawstatues.straw_statue.1: A player-shaped armor stand that can wear armor and hold items. Sneak while placing it for a random pose.
emi.info.strawstatues.straw_statue.2: Sneak right-click it with an empty hand to open its menu, where you can change its pose, size, rotation and the skin of any player by name. Right-clicking it with a Player Head also gives it that player's skin.
emi.info.storagedrawers.drawers.1: Stores a large amount of a single item in each slot, shown on its front. Right-click with an item to put it in, or double right-click to put in all of that item from your inventory. Left-click to take a single item, sneak left-click to take a stack. Hoppers can insert and extract items.
emi.info.storagedrawers.drawers.2: Each slot holds many stacks, fewer the more slots the Drawer has. Half Drawers hold half as much. Drawers keep their items when broken.
emi.info.storagedrawers.compacting_drawe: Stores a single material in its compressed and uncompressed forms, like blocks, ingots and nuggets, one per slot. All slots share the same stock: put in any form and take out any other, and it converts them for free.
The 2-slot version only holds two forms. Once emptied, it forgets the material and accepts a new one.
emi.info.storagedrawers.controller.1: Links all the Drawers touching it, and the ones touching those, into a single network, as long as they are not too far. Drawers and Trims next to each other carry the connection.
emi.info.storagedrawers.controller.2: Right-click with an item to put it in the network's Drawers, or double right-click to put in all of that item from your inventory. Hoppers and Pipes connected to it insert and extract from the whole network.
emi.info.storagedrawers.controller_io: Placed against a Drawer connected to a Controller, it gives Hoppers and Pipes access to the whole network from another spot. It can't be used by hand: right-click the Controller instead.
emi.info.storagedrawers.framing_table: Changes the look of Drawers and Trims: put one in with a full block for the sides, and optionally other blocks for the trim and the front, to get a Framed version that looks like those blocks.
emi.info.ecologics.coconut.1: Coconuts grow on Coconut trees and fall when ripe, hurting whoever they land on. Most smash on the ground, dropping Coconut Slices, and sometimes a Coconut Crab comes out. Some land intact, always when falling into water.
emi.info.ecologics.coconut.2: A placed Coconut can be broken with an Axe to open it into Coconut Slices.
emi.info.ecologics.coconut_slice: Eating a Coconut Slice removes all your effects, like Milk, and leaves a Coconut Husk, which can be used instead of a Bowl for stews.
emi.info.ecologics.crab_claw: Dropped by Coconut Crabs. It works as a pair of Shears with low durability, and lets you reach farther while held in the main hand.
emi.info.ecologics.sandcastle.1: Place it on Sand, or use it on Turtle Eggs to put them inside. Eggs in a Sandcastle are safe from mobs and hatch much faster.
emi.info.ecologics.sandcastle.2: Only players can break it by walking or jumping on it, which leaves the Turtle Eggs behind.
emi.info.ecologics.maple_syrup.1: Place a Spile on a Sappy Maple Log and hang a Bucket on it: it slowly fills with Maple Sap. When the Bucket is full, the log may run out of sap and turn into a normal Maple Log.
emi.info.ecologics.maple_syrup.2: Pour the Maple Sap into a Cauldron over a heat source (fire, a lit Campfire or Furnace, Magma, Lava...) and let it boil down, then fill a Glass Bottle with the Maple Syrup. The boiling sap hurts whoever stands in it.
emi.info.ecologics.prickly_pear: Prickly Pears grow on top of fully grown Cacti and can be planted on Cacti. Eating one cures Wither, but raw ones prick you.
emi.info.ecologics.pot.1: Click it with an item to drop one inside, until it's full. They can't be taken out: they drop when the Pot is broken.
emi.info.ecologics.pot.2: Each item put inside emits a redstone pulse, and Comparators read how many items it holds. Sneak right-click it with a Pickaxe to change its carving.
emi.info.ecologics.thin_ice: Thin Ice cracks when players and most mobs walk on it, and breaks into water after a few steps. Falling on it without Feather Falling cracks it and the ice around it.
emi.info.ecologics.penguin_feather: Dropped by baby Penguins when they grow up. Brewed into an Awkward Potion, it makes a Potion of Sliding, which makes you slide on any block as if it were ice.
emi.info.naturalist.capture_net.1: Use it on small critters like Butterflies, Caterpillars, Dragonflies, Fireflies, Bees, Ants, Snails, Crabs, Rats, Scorpions and Hedgehogs to catch them as an item. Use the item on a block to release the critter.
emi.info.naturalist.capture_net.2: With a Water Bucket in your inventory, it can also catch Cod into a Bucket of Cod. A caught Hedgehog can be thrown: it rolls into a ball and hurts whatever it hits.
emi.info.naturalist.knapsack: Use it on a baby animal to carry it inside, then use it on a block to release it there.
emi.info.map_atlases.atlas: Craft a Map with a Book and a Slime Ball or Honey Bottle to make an Atlas, then add Maps, Empty Maps or Paper to it in the crafting grid. While it's in your hotbar or hand it draws new maps as you explore, using up its Empty Maps. Use it to open a world map where you can place pins, or put it on a Lectern. With Antique Ink it becomes an Antique Atlas.
emi.info.heartstone.heartstone: Crafted in pairs: give the second one to a friend. Right-click it to send a particle trail towards the player holding the other one, who glows when you get close.
emi.info.naturalist.whistle: Use it on one of your tamed animals to switch between following you and wandering freely.
emi.info.naturalist.ant_hill.1: Breaking the Ant Hill chamber where the queen lives drops a Queen Ant. Breaking a chamber with ants inside makes them come out and attack you.
emi.info.naturalist.ant_hill.2: Use a Queen Ant on the ground to start your own Ant Hill. Its ants store the food they gather inside, which drops when the chamber is broken.
emi.info.naturalist.glow_goop: Cooked from Glow Berries in a Smoker or on a Campfire, and dropped by Fireflies. Place it to light up an area, even underwater; stacking more in the same spot makes it brighter. It can also be turned into Spectral Arrows at the Fletching Table.
emi.info.naturalist.froglass: Dropped when a Frog eats a Dragonfly. Its color depends on the Dragonfly's.
emi.info.naturalist.snail_shell: Dropped by Snails. Place it as a decoration, dye it in the crafting grid, or put a small plant in it like in a Flower Pot. Crafted with Calcite into Shellstone.
emi.info.naturalist.starfish: Dropped by Starfish. It can be placed on any side of a block, even underwater.
emi.info.naturalist.antler: Dropped by Deer. Brewed into an Awkward Potion, it makes a Potion of the Forest Dasher, which gives Speed and Weakness.
emi.info.naturalist.scorpion_poison_glan: Dropped by Scorpions. Brewed into an Awkward Potion, it makes a Potion of Antivenom, which cures Poison.
emi.info.naturalist.hide: Dropped by Boars, Rhinos, Elephants and Komodo Dragons. Craft it into a Knapsack, or smelt it into Leather.
emi.info.naturalist.fur: Shear an adult Bear to get it without hurting it: the fur grows back over time. Also dropped by Lions, Tigers and Mammoths.
emi.info.naturalist.eggs: Laid by Alligators, Tortoises and Ostriches after breeding. They hatch over time, but can break when walked or fallen on. Only Silk Touch picks them up.
emi.info.naturalist.duck_egg: Laid by Ducks. Throw it to sometimes hatch a Duckling, or use it instead of an Egg in Cakes and Pumpkin Pies.
emi.info.naturalist.chrysalis: Caterpillars turn into a Chrysalis on the side of a log, which later hatches into a Butterfly. Only Shears or Silk Touch pick it up.
emi.info.naturalist.music_discs: "Wild Ones" is sometimes carried by Foxes. "Death by Hogs" is sometimes dropped by Boars when they kill a player.
emi.info.naturalist.fat: Dropped by Boars, Mammoths and Whales.
emi.info.naturalist.tooth: Dropped by Alligators, Great White Sharks, Lions, Tigers and Snakes.
emi.info.naturalist.morsel: A small piece of meat dropped by Hedgehogs, Lizards, Rats, Snakes and Vultures. Tigers and Komodo Dragons like it.
emi.info.naturalist.lizard_tail: A Lizard drops its tail when badly hurt. The tail wriggles on the ground: hit it to pick it up.
Found inside Pale Oak trees in the Pale Garden. When placed between two Pale Oak Logs lined up with it, it wakes up at night and spawns a Creaking.
Every hit on its Creaking makes Resin Clumps grow on the blocks around the heart. Break the Creaking Heart to destroy its Creaking.
emi.info.vanillabackport.resin_clump: Grows around a Creaking Heart when its Creaking is hit. Place it on any side of a block, or smelt it into Resin Bricks.
emi.info.vanillabackport.eyeblossom: Opens at night and closes during the day. Open ones make Orange Dye and closed ones Gray Dye; in Suspicious Stew they give Blindness (open) or Nausea (closed).
emi.info.vanillabackport.firefly_bush: Gives off a little light, and fireflies fly around it in the dark.
emi.info.vanillabackport.segmented_plant: Use more on one already placed to fill the block a bit more each time.
emi.info.vanillabackport.dried_ghast: Found in Nether Fossils and given by Piglins when bartering. Place it in water: it slowly rehydrates and turns into a Ghastling, which grows into a Happy Ghast.
emi.info.vanillabackport.harness: Put it on an adult Happy Ghast to ride it. Use Shears to take it off.
emi.info.vanillabackport.copper_chest: A chest that oxidizes like other copper blocks. Copper Golems take items out of Copper Chests and sort them into nearby chests.
emi.info.vanillabackport.copper_golem_st: A Copper Golem that is fully oxidized can turn into a statue. Use it with an empty hand to change its pose; a Comparator reads a different signal for each pose.
Scrape it with an Axe until all the oxidation is gone to bring the Copper Golem back. Wax it with a Honeycomb to keep it as a decoration.
emi.info.vanillabackport.lightning_rod.1: Oxidizes like other copper blocks; wax it with a Honeycomb to stop it.
emi.info.vanillabackport.lightning_rod.2: Known issue: a new, unwaxed Lightning Rod doesn't attract lightning (Vanilla Backport bug). Wax it with a Honeycomb: waxed and oxidized ones work.
emi.info.vanillabackport.shelf.1: Holds a few items on its front. Use an item on a slot to place or swap it, or an empty hand to take it.
emi.info.vanillabackport.shelf.2: When powered by redstone, using it swaps all its items with your hotbar. Powered Shelves placed side by side connect and swap more slots together.
emi.info.vanillabackport.straw_bed: Lets you sleep anywhere, but doesn't set your spawn point and breaks when you wake up.
emi.info.vanillabackport.cushion: Place it on top of a block and use it to sit down.
emi.info.vanillabackport.shelf_mushroom: Placed on the side of a block. Landing on it bounces you back up and lessens fall damage. Use Bone Meal to make it bigger.
emi.info.vanillabackport.potent_sulfur.1: Found in Sulfur Caves. Under water it releases a gas that gives Nausea nearby.
emi.info.vanillabackport.potent_sulfur.2: With a Magma Block below it, it turns into a geyser that erupts from time to time and pushes things upward; with Lava below, it erupts without stopping. The deeper the water above it, the higher it pushes.
emi.info.vanillabackport.sulfur_spike: Found in Sulfur Caves. Works like Pointed Dripstone.
emi.info.vanillabackport.sulfur_cube.1: A Sulfur Cube caught in a Bucket, together with the block it swallowed. Only adults can be caught. Use it to release the Sulfur Cube.
emi.info.vanillabackport.nautilus_armor: Armor for a tamed Nautilus or Zombie Nautilus. On a Zombie Nautilus it also keeps it from burning in sunlight, but wears out instead.
emi.info.vanillabackport.music_discs: "Tears" is dropped by a Ghast killed by its own fireball sent back at it. "Lava Chicken" is dropped by a baby Zombie riding a Chicken when a player kills it. "Bounce" is found in Abandoned Mineshaft chests.
emi.info.minecraft.sculk_sensor.1: Detects vibrations nearby and emits a redstone signal, stronger the closer the vibration. A Comparator instead reads its frequency, which depends on what caused the vibration:
emi.info.minecraft.sculk_sensor.2: 1: walking, swimming, flying. 2: projectiles landing, falling on the ground, splashing. 3: finishing using an item, shooting, playing a Goat Horn. 4: other mob actions, gliding with an Elytra, unequipping. 5: getting off a mob or vehicle, equipping. 6: getting on a mob or vehicle (Minecarts and Boats too), interacting with or shearing a mob. 7: taking damage.
emi.info.minecraft.sculk_sensor.3: 8: eating, drinking. 9: closing containers, doors and trapdoors, deactivating or detaching blocks. 10: opening them, activating or attaching blocks, priming TNT, playing Note Blocks. 11: blocks changing state. 12: breaking blocks, picking up fluids. 13: placing blocks and fluids. 14: placing entities, lightning, teleporting. 15: deaths and explosions.
emi.info.minecraft.sculk_sensor.4: Wool blocks the vibrations passing through it, and sneaking doesn't make any. An Amethyst Block next to an activated sensor re-emits the vibration with the same frequency.
emi.info.minecraft.calibrated_sculk_sens: Works like a Sculk Sensor with a longer range, but the redstone signal entering it from the side marked by the amethyst sets the only frequency it reacts to. With no input, it reacts to every vibration.
emi.info.minecraft.wet_sponge: Found in Ocean Monuments and dropped by Elder Guardians: the stronger they are, the more they drop.
emi.info.minecraft.compass: Points to the world spawn point. Use it on a Lodestone to make it point to that block instead. In the Nether and the End it spins randomly.
emi.info.minecraft.lodestone: Use a Compass on it to make the Compass point to this Lodestone, even in the Nether. If the Lodestone is broken, the Compass stops pointing anywhere. Clicking it with a Map marks it on the Map.
emi.info.minecraft.recovery_compass: Points to where you last died, as long as you are in the same dimension: that's where the Totem of Holding with your items is waiting. While you carry it, your Maps also show a marker at that spot.
emi.info.minecraft.map.1: Use an Empty Map to draw the area around you: it keeps filling in as you explore while holding it. In a Cartography Table you can make it cover a larger area, copy it or lock it.
emi.info.minecraft.map.2: Use a Map on a Banner to add a marker for it, and on a Beacon, Lodestone, Respawn Anchor, bed, Conduit or portal to mark that block. Use it on a Cauldron with water to wash it back into an Empty Map.
emi.info.minecraft.goat_horn: Goats drop one when they ram a solid block such as stone, logs, ores or ice instead of their target. Also found in chests of Pillager Outposts, Illager Manors and some ruins. Each horn plays a different sound that can be heard from far away, and screaming Goats drop different horns.
emi.info.minecraft.obsidian: Ready to go deeper? Build a frame of Obsidian 4 blocks wide and 5 tall and light it with Flint and Steel or a Fire Charge to open a Nether Portal: in the Overworld its corners must be Crying Obsidian.
emi.info.minecraft.spyglass: Hold use to look through it and zoom in on things far away, like distant mobs, structures or the terrain ahead.
emi.info.minecraft.bundle: Holds different kinds of items in a single slot, up to one stack's worth: items that stack to 16 take more room, unstackable ones fill it alone. In the inventory, right-click an item with the Bundle (or the Bundle with an item) to put it in, and right-click an empty slot with it to take the last item out. Using it in hand drops everything inside.
emi.info.minecraft.piston.1: When powered, pushes the blocks in front of it, up to 12 in a row. A Sticky Piston also pulls back the block it touches. Slime and Honey Blocks drag along the blocks stuck to them, but don't stick to each other.
emi.info.minecraft.piston.2: Obsidian, Crying Obsidian, Bedrock, Respawn Anchors, Spawners, Ender Chests, Enchanting Tables and Trapped Chests can't be moved. Plants, torches and other fragile blocks break instead.
emi.info.minecraft.observer: Watches the block its face points at: when that block changes (placed, broken, grown, opened...), it sends a short redstone pulse out of its back.
emi.info.minecraft.comparator.1: Placed behind a container, it emits a signal that gets stronger the fuller the container is. It also reads other blocks, such as a Cake, a Composter, a Cauldron, the page of a Lectern's book, a Jukebox's disc or an Item Frame's rotation.
emi.info.minecraft.comparator.2: Right-click it to switch mode. With the front torch off it passes the signal from behind only if it's not weaker than the one from the sides; with the torch on it subtracts the side signal from it.
emi.info.minecraft.repeater: Carries a redstone signal forward in one direction only, bringing it back to full strength. Right-click it to add delay. A powered Repeater or Comparator pointing into its side locks it in its current state.
emi.info.minecraft.target: Emits a redstone signal when hit by an arrow, a trident or another projectile: the closer to the center, the stronger the signal. Redstone Dust always connects to it.
emi.info.minecraft.daylight_detector: Emits a redstone signal during the day, stronger when the sun is high. Right-click it to invert it, so it gives a signal at night instead.
emi.info.minecraft.note_block: Plays a note when hit or powered by redstone; right-click it to raise the pitch. The block below picks the instrument: wood, stone, sand, glass, wool, gold and many others each sound different. A mob head on top makes it play that mob's sound, otherwise the block above must be air.
emi.info.minecraft.sculk_shrieker: Shrieks when stepped on or when a nearby Sculk Sensor picks up a vibration. The ones in Ancient Cities also give Darkness to nearby players and, after a few shrieks, summon the Warden. The ones you place only shriek.
emi.info.minecraft.crafter: Crafts on its own: fill its grid by hand or with Hoppers, which spread the items across the slots, and each redstone pulse crafts one result, thrown out of the front or put into the container it faces. Click a slot to disable it, so it stays empty for the recipe. A Comparator reads how many slots are filled.
emi.info.minecraft.hopper: Collects items that fall on it or sit in a container above it and passes them into the container its narrow end points to, chosen when you place it. A redstone signal stops it. A Minecart with Hopper picks up items the same way while riding on rails, and a Hopper under the rails can empty it.
emi.info.minecraft.dropper: When powered, throws out one item from inside, or pushes it into the container it faces: useful to move items upward or sideways.
emi.info.minecraft.dispenser.1: When powered, uses one item from inside instead of just dropping it: it shoots arrows, Fire Charges and other projectiles, places and picks up water and lava with buckets, lights fires with Flint and Steel, primes TNT, shears Sheep, uses Bone Meal, puts armor on whoever is in front and places boats, minecarts and Shulker Boxes.
emi.info.minecraft.dispenser.2: In this pack it also places most blocks, strips logs and scrapes copper with an Axe, throws Ender Pearls and empties Bundles. Other items are dropped like a Dropper does.
emi.info.minecraft.detector_rail: Emits a redstone signal while a minecart is on it. A Comparator next to it reads how full the minecart's container is.
emi.info.minecraft.activator_rail: When powered, activates the minecarts passing over it: Minecarts with TNT explode, Minecarts with Hopper stop collecting and riders are thrown off.
emi.info.minecraft.tripwire_hook: Place two Tripwire Hooks facing each other and connect them with String: when someone walks through the String, both hooks emit a redstone signal. Cutting it with Shears doesn't set it off.
emi.info.minecraft.lightning_rod: During thunderstorms it draws in lightning that would strike nearby, keeping it away from flammable buildings, and emits a redstone signal when hit. A strike also removes the oxidation from it and the copper around it.
emi.info.minecraft.conduit: Place it underwater at the center of a frame of Prismarine, Prismarine Bricks, Dark Prismarine or Sea Lanterns: three hollow 5x5 squares crossing around it, one for each direction. It needs water all around it and turns on with at least 16 frame blocks; players in the water nearby get Conduit Power, which lets them breathe and see clearly. A bigger frame reaches farther, and with the full frame of 42 blocks it also attacks hostile mobs close to it.
emi.info.minecraft.respawn_anchor: Sets your respawn point in the Nether, where Beds explode. Charge it with Glowstone, then right-click it to set your spawn: each respawn uses one charge. Right-clicking a charged Anchor in the Overworld or the End makes it explode violently.
emi.info.minecraft.lectern: Holds a book that everyone can read. Turning a page emits a short redstone pulse, and a Comparator reads which page is open.
emi.info.minecraft.jukebox: Plays a Music Disc. While playing it emits a redstone signal, and a Comparator reads which disc is in it.
emi.info.minecraft.cauldron: Slowly fills with water when it rains, or with Powder Snow when it snows. Pointed Dripstone hanging above it also drips water or lava into it, when that liquid is on top of the block the Dripstone hangs from.
emi.info.minecraft.bell: Ringing it makes nearby Illagers glow for a while, so you can find them during a raid, and sends nearby villagers indoors.
emi.info.minecraft.brewing_stand: Brews potions using Blaze Powder as fuel (from the Blaze Rods dropped by Blazes in Nether Fortresses). Put up to three Water Bottles at the bottom, filled from any water, and an ingredient at the top. Most potions start from Nether Wart, which gives an Awkward Potion; then Redstone makes the effect last longer, Glowstone makes it stronger, a Fermented Spider Eye turns it into a harmful version, Gunpowder makes it a Splash Potion to throw and Dragon's Breath a Lingering one. Every step is shown in EMI.
emi.info.minecraft.bee_nest: Home of Bees. When it's full of honey, use a Glass Bottle on it to get Honey or Shears to get Honeycombs: do it with a lit Campfire under it, or the bees get angry and sting. Bee Nests are found on trees in flowery biomes, the Beehive is the crafted version.
emi.info.minecraft.honeycomb: Use it on copper blocks to wax them, so they stop oxidizing. An Axe scrapes the wax off.
emi.info.minecraft.honey_block: Mobs and players on it move slowly and can barely jump. It softens falls, and you slide slowly down its sides.
emi.info.minecraft.ender_chest: All Ender Chests share the same inventory, separate for each player: what you put in one can be taken out of any other, anywhere, even in other dimensions. Breaking it doesn't lose the items stored.
emi.info.minecraft.netherite_upgrade_smi: Found in Bastion Remnant chests and in other Nether structures, and dropped by the stronger Withers.
emi.info.minecraft.sentry_armor_trim_smi: Found in Pillager Outpost, Illager Manor and Stronghold chests, and in some dungeons.
emi.info.minecraft.wild_armor_trim_smith: Found in Jungle Temple chests and Suspicious blocks, and in some dungeons.
emi.info.minecraft.coast_armor_trim_smit: Found in Shipwreck and Stronghold chests.
emi.info.minecraft.dune_armor_trim_smith: Found in Desert Temple chests and Suspicious Sand, and on some bridges in the Badlands.
emi.info.minecraft.eye_armor_trim_smithi: Found in Stronghold chests, and in some dungeons in cold biomes.
emi.info.minecraft.ward_armor_trim_smith: Found in Ancient City chests and Suspicious blocks, and in some dungeons.
emi.info.minecraft.silence_armor_trim_sm: Found in Ancient City chests and Suspicious blocks. Very rare.
emi.info.minecraft.snout_armor_trim_smit: Found in Bastion Remnant chests and in other Nether structures.
emi.info.minecraft.rib_armor_trim_smithi: Found in Nether Fortress chests, in other Nether structures, in Nether Trials and in Strongholds.
emi.info.minecraft.flow_armor_trim_smith: Found in Ominous Vaults in Trial Chambers.
emi.info.minecraft.wayfinder_armor_trim_: Found by brushing Suspicious Gravel in Trail Ruins, and in some dungeons.
emi.info.minecraft.raiser_armor_trim_smi: Found by brushing Suspicious Gravel in Trail Ruins, and in some dungeons.
emi.info.minecraft.shaper_armor_trim_smi: Found by brushing Suspicious Gravel in Trail Ruins, and in some dungeons.
emi.info.minecraft.host_armor_trim_smith: Found by brushing Suspicious Gravel in Trail Ruins, and in some dungeons.
emi.info.minecraft.echo_shard: Found in Ancient City chests and Suspicious blocks, deep underground in the Deep Dark.
emi.info.minecraft.disc_fragment_5: Found in Ancient City chests and Suspicious blocks.
emi.info.minecraft.dragon_breath: Collected with a Glass Bottle from the purple cloud left by the Ender Dragon's breath attack. Also found in some Ancient City chests.
emi.info.minecraft.nautilus_shell: Caught while fishing, found in Ocean Ruins, and dropped by Nautiluses, Crabs and Drowned holding one.
emi.info.minecraft.sniffer_egg: Found by brushing Suspicious Sand in Warm Ocean Ruins and Jungle Temples. Placed down, it hatches into a Sniffer after a while, sooner on a Moss Block. Two Sniffers that fall in love lay a new egg.
emi.info.minecraft.breeze_rod: Dropped by Breezes, found in Trial Chambers.
emi.info.minecraft.heavy_core: Found in Ominous Vaults in Trial Chambers and in some Nether arenas. Very rare.
emi.info.minecraft.trial_spawner: Found in Trial Chambers. When players come close it spawns waves of mobs, more with more players; once they're all defeated it drops rewards and a Trial Key, then rests for a while. Under Trial Omen it turns Ominous: stronger mobs, harmful items dropped on you from above, and Ominous Trial Keys as reward.
emi.info.minecraft.vault: Found in Trial Chambers. Use a Trial Key on it to get a reward, or an Ominous Trial Key on an Ominous Vault. Each Vault gives its reward only once to each player.
emi.info.minecraft.trial_key: Dropped by Trial Spawners when all their mobs are defeated, in Trial Chambers and in similar structures in the Nether and in Ocean Monuments. Also found in some of their chests and Decorated Pots. Opens a Vault.
emi.info.minecraft.ominous_trial_key: Dropped by Ominous Trial Spawners when all their mobs are defeated. Opens an Ominous Vault, which gives better rewards.
emi.info.minecraft.ominous_bottle: Dropped by Raid Captains, the Pillagers carrying a banner, and found in Trial Chamber Vaults. Drinking it gives Bad Omen: in a village it starts a Raid, in a Trial Chamber it turns into Trial Omen, which makes the Trial Spawners Ominous.
emi.info.minecraft.phantom_membrane: Dropped by Phantoms. A Cat sleeping on your bed sometimes brings one in the morning.
emi.info.minecraft.nether_star: Dropped by the Wither, a boss you build: four Soul Sand or Soul Soil in a T shape with three Wither Skeleton Skulls on top. The skulls are dropped by Wither Skeletons in Nether Fortresses. Build it far from your base, as it destroys blocks.
emi.info.minecraft.wither_rose: Grows where the Wither kills a mob. Anyone walking into it gets Wither.
emi.info.minecraft.ancient_debris: Found deep in the Nether, usually buried in Netherrack, and in Bastion Remnant chests and other Nether structures. Needs a Diamond Pickaxe, and doesn't burn in lava or fire.
emi.info.minecraft.ender_eye: Throw an Eye of Ender and it flies toward the nearest Stronghold, then drops or breaks. In the Stronghold's portal room, put an Eye of Ender in each End Portal Frame to open the portal to the End, where the Ender Dragon lives.
emi.info.minecraft.end_crystal: Placed on Obsidian or Bedrock, it explodes when hit. In the End the crystals on top of the pillars heal the Ender Dragon, so destroy them first. Four placed on the sides of the exit portal bring the Dragon back.
emi.info.minecraft.amethyst: Found in Amethyst Geodes, hollow underground spheres lined with Calcite. Budding Amethyst slowly grows buds on its free sides: a fully grown Amethyst Cluster drops Amethyst Shards when broken, smaller buds drop nothing. Budding Amethyst can't be picked up, mining it destroys it.
emi.info.minecraft.music_discs: Played in a Jukebox. Most Music Discs are dropped by Creepers killed by a Skeleton or a Stray, and 13 and Cat are also found in Dungeons. Others come only from structures: Pigstep from Bastion Remnants, Otherside from Dungeons, Strongholds and Ancient Cities, Relic from Suspicious Gravel in Trail Ruins, Precipice from Trial Chamber Vaults, Creator from Ominous Vaults, Creator (Music Box) from Decorated Pots in Trial Chambers, and 5 from the Disc Fragments found in Ancient Cities.
emi.info.minecraft.elytra: Wings worn in the chest slot. Jump, then press jump again while falling to glide; tilt down to gain speed, up to slow down. Using a Firework Rocket while gliding gives a boost. Found in item frames on End Ships, the flying ships near some End Cities in the outer islands of the End.
emi.info.minecraft.mace: Hitting a mob while falling makes a smash attack: the longer the fall, the more damage it deals, and it cancels your fall damage. Throw a Wind Charge at your feet to bounce up again for the next hit. Besides crafting it, it's found in the vaults of Nether Trials.
emi.info.minecraft.trident: Hold use and release to throw it, then pick it up again; if it falls into the void it comes back to you. Crafted from Trident Fragments, dropped by Drowned killed by a player and by Elder Guardians. Some Drowned also hold a Trident and can drop it, and it's found in Trial Chamber vaults, in the vaults of Ocean Monuments and in Stronghold sewers.
emi.info.minecraft.wind_charge: Throw it to make a burst of wind that pushes away mobs, players and you too: throw it at your feet to jump high, and the burst also cancels fall damage. It toggles doors, trapdoors, buttons and levers it hits. Besides crafting it from Breeze Rods, it's found in Trial Chamber vaults and in some Nether structures.
emi.info.universalbonemeal.bone_meal: Bone Meal also works on Nether Wart, Vines and Chorus Flowers. On small flowers, Dead Bushes and Lily Pads it spreads more of them around. On a fully grown Melon or Pumpkin stem it makes the fruit grow, on Podzol it grows Ferns and Sweet Berry Bushes, and on Mycelium it grows mushrooms. On Coral in a Warm Ocean, with enough room above, it grows a tree of coral blocks.
emi.info.minecraft.nether_wart: Grows only on Soul Sand, in any dimension. Found in Nether Fortresses and in the chests of other Nether structures and of Nether Trials. It's the base of almost every potion.
emi.info.minecraft.chorus_fruit: Chorus Plants grow on the outer islands of the End, reached through the gateway that opens after killing the Ender Dragon. Breaking them drops Chorus Fruit: eating it teleports you to a random spot nearby, which can save you from a fall. A Chorus Flower planted on End Stone grows into a new plant.
emi.info.minecraft.torchflower_seeds: Ancient seeds that Sniffers dig out of grass and dirt (see the Sniffer Egg). Planted on Farmland they grow into a Torchflower or a Pitcher Plant. Torchflower Seeds are also what makes two Sniffers lay an egg.
emi.info.minecraft.frogspawn: Laid on water by Frogs after mating, it hatches into Tadpoles. A Tadpole grows into a Frog whose color depends on the biome: orange in temperate biomes, white in warm ones and green in cold ones. Frogs eat small Magma Cubes and drop a Froglight: Ochre from orange Frogs, Pearlescent from white ones and Verdant from green ones.
emi.info.minecraft.carrot_on_a_stick: Hold it while riding a saddled Pig to steer it; using it gives a short burst of speed and wears it out. The Warped Fungus on a Stick does the same with a saddled Strider, which walks on lava in the Nether.
emi.info.quark.crate: Hoppers and Pipes can insert and extract items. Breaking it spills its contents on the ground.
emi.info.quark.magnet.1: It pushes the blocks in front of it away and pulls the ones behind it closer, both in the direction it faces. It also moves dropped iron and copper items and mobs wearing iron armor.
emi.info.quark.magnet.2: A Stonecutter moved by a Magnet drops the blocks it cuts as if mined with Silk Touch. Wax a Magnet with a Honeycomb to hide its particles.
emi.info.quark.pipe.1: Items that reach an open end come out of it. Pipes connect by themselves to every adjacent Pipe and container, and their sides can't be closed. Right-click a Pipe with Glass to encase it, or with a Stick to refresh the connections of the whole network if they look wrong.
emi.info.tiny_takeover_backport.golden_d: Use it on a baby animal to stop it from growing up. Use it again to let it grow.
emi.info.vibrantparrots.parrot_eggs: Laid by a tamed Parrot some time after it falls in love, in its own color. Throw the egg to hatch a chick.
emi.info.vibrantparrots.bird_cage: Use it on a Parrot you tamed to carry it around in the cage, and use it again to let the Parrot out, like a Bucket with fish.
emi.info.runeenchanting.rune.librarian: Librarians sell Runes, which are never Curses.
advancements.fieldguide.root.description: Get a Spyglass and look at mobs through it to add them to your Field Guide, opened with B
fieldguide.minecraft.bogged.description:
Lives in Mangrove Swamps and comes out of the trial spawners of Trial Chambers and Adventure Dungeons. Some are found in Jungle Temples.

Skeletons shoot from a long range and back away if you get close, but aren't very accurate. They wear armor more often under a full moon and deep underground, and they come in different sizes. They climb ladders, some ride other mobs and leaders call others to help.
fieldguide.minecraft.breeze.description: Only comes out of the trial spawners of Trial Chambers and Hellish Trials.
fieldguide.minecraft.cave_spider.descrip: Lives in Sulfur Caves and comes from the spawners in Mineshafts and Strongholds. Some of the Spiders in caves are Cave Spiders instead. It barely takes fall damage, sometimes rides other mobs and throws webs that slow you down and poison you.
fieldguide.minecraft.creeper.description:
Lives almost everywhere in the Overworld. Many can blow up through walls, some keep walking while lit and some circle around you. A few blast holes in walls to let other monsters in, and rarely one is Angry, with a much bigger explosion.

Now and then one lights itself and launches at you. It doesn't light from falling, but another explosion can set it off.
fieldguide.minecraft.drowned.description:
Lives in oceans, rivers and Dripstone Caves. It attacks during the day too and only starts burning in sunlight after a while. It jumps out of water, swims fast, grabs you to drag you underwater and steals your air when it hits. In oceans, half of them ride a Zombie Nautilus.

Zombies come in different sizes. They climb ladders, lunge at you, sprint when close and bite back if you hit them without a weapon. Some carry a Fishing Rod to pull you in or Ender Pearls to reach you, some pick up other mobs and throw them at you, and some ride other mobs. Leaders call others to help.

They're better equipped under a full moon, under the open sky and deep underground. In caves some are miners that dig their way to you, more often the deeper you go.
fieldguide.minecraft.enderman.descriptio: Lives almost everywhere, in all three dimensions. It gets angry even if you look at it from the side and climbs ladders. If you attack it from where it can't reach, it teleports. It can also teleport other monsters next to you.
fieldguide.minecraft.endermite.descripti: Sometimes comes out of a thrown Ender Pearl. Also found in Strongholds and in the spawners of some ruins.
fieldguide.minecraft.evoker.description: Lives in Woodland Mansions and joins raids. Its Vexes die with it. It opens doors and slowly heals over time.
fieldguide.minecraft.guardian.descriptio: Comes out of the trial spawners of Ocean Monuments, and also lives deep down in deep oceans: those are smaller and much weaker. It deals magic damage.
fieldguide.minecraft.husk.description:
Lives in Deserts and is found in Desert Temples. In Deserts it can ride a Camel Husk, with a Parched behind it.

Zombies come in different sizes. They climb ladders, lunge at you, sprint when close and bite back if you hit them without a weapon. Some carry a Fishing Rod to pull you in or Ender Pearls to reach you, some pick up other mobs and throw them at you, and some ride other mobs. Leaders call others to help.

They're better equipped under a full moon, under the open sky and deep underground. In caves some are miners that dig their way to you, more often the deeper you go.
fieldguide.minecraft.phantom.description: Comes at night for players who are very tired and under the open sky, and also lives in some Nether biomes. Comes in random sizes, some very big. Its hits slow you down more and more and make you fall slowly, and it grabs you and carries you up in the air until you hit it back.
fieldguide.minecraft.pillager.descriptio: Lives in Pillager Outposts and Woodland Mansions, and comes in patrols and raids. It shoots accurately from a long range, sometimes keeps its distance, opens doors and slowly heals over time.
fieldguide.minecraft.ravager.description: Comes with raids, and some are kept in Woodland Mansions. It slowly heals over time.
fieldguide.minecraft.silverfish.descript: Hides in infested blocks in Strongholds and mountains, and comes from Stronghold spawners and Urns broken in caves. When hurt, it wakes up many Silverfish hiding nearby.
fieldguide.minecraft.skeleton.descriptio:
Lives almost everywhere in the Overworld and in some Nether biomes, but not in Nether Fortresses. Also comes from Dungeon spawners. Rarely, one has a Quiver.

Skeletons shoot from a long range and back away if you get close, but aren't very accurate. They wear armor more often under a full moon and deep underground, and they come in different sizes. They climb ladders, some ride other mobs and leaders call others to help.
fieldguide.minecraft.slime.description: Lives underground in slime chunks and in swamps, and comes out of Urns broken in caves. It can be huge, jumps often and only hurts when it jumps at you or lands on you, not by touching you. It takes no fall damage. Small ones can be picked up with a Bucket, and a Slime killed on a Magma Block splits into Magma Cubes.
fieldguide.minecraft.spider.description: Lives almost everywhere in the Overworld and comes from Dungeon spawners. It barely takes fall damage and other monsters sometimes ride it. It throws webs that slow you down.
fieldguide.minecraft.stray.description:
Lives in Snowy Plains and Ice Spikes, and comes out of the trial spawners of Trial Chambers and Adventure Dungeons.

Skeletons shoot from a long range and back away if you get close, but aren't very accurate. They wear armor more often under a full moon and deep underground, and they come in different sizes. They climb ladders, some ride other mobs and leaders call others to help.
fieldguide.minecraft.vex.description: Summoned by Evokers, and dies with its Evoker. Also comes from spawners in Nether Sanctums. It goes down in a few hits.
fieldguide.minecraft.vindicator.descript: Lives in Woodland Mansions and joins raids. It lunges at you, opens doors and slowly heals over time.
fieldguide.minecraft.warden.description: Summoned by the Sculk Shriekers of Ancient Cities, in the Deep Dark. Two warnings are enough to summon it, and they take a long time to wear off. It steps up full blocks, hears you from far away and its Darkness and Sonic Boom have a long reach.
fieldguide.minecraft.witch.description: Lives almost everywhere in the Overworld and in Swamp Huts, and joins raids. It throws many kinds of potions quickly and from far away, drinks potions often and throws helpful ones at nearby monsters. It sometimes keeps its distance and slowly heals over time.
fieldguide.minecraft.zombie.description:
Lives almost everywhere in the Overworld and comes from Dungeon spawners. Some nights, a horde of Zombies comes for a player who has spent a long time in the same area.

Zombies come in different sizes. They climb ladders, lunge at you, sprint when close and bite back if you hit them without a weapon. Some carry a Fishing Rod to pull you in or Ender Pearls to reach you, some pick up other mobs and throw them at you, and some ride other mobs. Leaders call others to help.

They're better equipped under a full moon, under the open sky and deep underground. In caves some are miners that dig their way to you, more often the deeper you go.
fieldguide.minecraft.zombie_villager.des:
Lives almost everywhere in the Overworld and fills the abandoned villages; a few are also in Igloos and Strongholds. Those in structures don't burn in sunlight. A Villager killed by a Zombie always turns into one.

Curing them is the only way to get Villagers: give a Golden Carrot to one under Weakness. Once cured, it needs a day to recover before it trades or works. Cured Nitwits become normal Villagers that can take a job.

Zombies come in different sizes. They climb ladders, lunge at you, sprint when close and bite back if you hit them without a weapon. Some carry a Fishing Rod to pull you in or Ender Pearls to reach you, some pick up other mobs and throw them at you, and some ride other mobs. Leaders call others to help.

They're better equipped under a full moon, under the open sky and deep underground. In caves some are miners that dig their way to you, more often the deeper you go.
fieldguide.minecraft.blaze.description: Lives in Nether Fortresses and other Nether structures, and in Infernal Dunes and Volcanic Deltas. Also comes from spawners and from the trial spawners of Hellish Trials. Its bursts of fireballs vary in length and speed, sometimes with two fireballs at a time.
fieldguide.minecraft.elder_guardian.desc: Lives in Ocean Monuments, some waiting in place and some coming out of trial spawners. It has extra absorption hearts, heals a little with each hit and calls Elder Minions, weaker Guardians that swim faster. Every Elder Guardian killed makes the others nearby stronger: tougher, quicker to attack and to call minions.
fieldguide.minecraft.ghast.description: Lives in Nether Wastes, Soul Sand Valleys, Basalt Deltas and other open Nether biomes. It sometimes shoots several fireballs in a row, and some keep shooting even when they can't see you, faster, to blast through cover.
fieldguide.minecraft.hoglin.description:
Lives in Crimson Forests and Bastion Remnants. Taken to the Overworld or the End, it turns into a Zoglin.

Search #hoglin_food in EMI to see what it eats.

It can't be bred by hand: adults fall in love on their own now and then, much more often for a while after you feed them, and less in crowded areas. Breeding can fail and sometimes gives twins.
fieldguide.minecraft.magma_cube.descript: Lives in Basalt Deltas, Nether Wastes and many other Nether biomes, and in Nether Fortresses and other Nether structures, some from spawners. It can be huge, jumps often, moves fast in lava and only hurts when it jumps at you or lands on you, not by touching you. A Slime killed on a Magma Block splits into Magma Cubes.
fieldguide.minecraft.piglin.description: Lives in Crimson Forests, Nether Wastes and Ash Barrens, and in Bastion Remnants and other Nether structures. It climbs ladders, lunges at you and sprints when close.
fieldguide.minecraft.piglin_brute.descri: Only found in Bastion Remnants and a few other Nether structures, some from spawners. It climbs ladders, lunges at you and sprints when close.
fieldguide.minecraft.shulker.description: Lives in End Cities and End Gate Fortresses. It's very armored when closed, less when partway open and a little when open. Once badly hurt it only opens partway while shooting, and when almost dead it stays closed if you're close. Its bullets give a strong, short Levitation and vanish when it dies.
fieldguide.minecraft.strider.description:
Lives on the lava seas of almost every Nether biome.

Search #strider_food in EMI to see what it eats.

It can't be bred by hand: adults fall in love on their own now and then, much more often for a while after you feed them, and less in crowded areas. Breeding can fail and sometimes gives twins.
fieldguide.minecraft.wither_skeleton.des: Lives in Nether Fortresses and other Nether structures, and in Withered Forests. It climbs ladders, lunges at you and sprints when close. Wither Skeletons come in different sizes. Some carry a Bow: they shoot from a long range, back away if you get close and their arrows wither you instead of setting you on fire.
fieldguide.minecraft.zoglin.description: A Hoglin taken to the Overworld or the End turns into one. Also comes from spawners in some ruins.
fieldguide.minecraft.zombified_piglin.de: Lives in Nether Wastes and Crimson Forests, and in Nether Fortresses and other Nether structures. Zombified Piglins come in different sizes. It climbs ladders, lunges at you, sprints when close and bites back if you hit it without a weapon. It sometimes picks up other mobs and throws them at you, and sometimes rides other mobs.
fieldguide.minecraft.ender_dragon.descri:
Lives in the End and can be respawned with four End Crystals on the exit portal. Respawning it with four Corrupted End Crystals, made with a Dragon Egg, summons the much stronger Corrupted Ender Dragon.

It heals over time and from the End Crystals, more from Corrupted ones, and destroying a crystal while it's healing the Dragon hurts it. Crystals can't be set off by other explosions, many towers are caged and some hide a crystal inside. Once it's below half health, it can bring crystals back, together with Phantoms.

Hitting it in flight hurts it more than when it's perched, and explosions barely hurt it. Damage makes it angry, faster and more aggressive. It shoots acid balls that leave a lingering cloud, charges at you, calls Shulker minions and sometimes stops to charge a blast that throws you far away.
fieldguide.minecraft.wither.description:
Built from four Soul Sand or Soul Soil and three Wither Skeleton Skulls. Putting Corrupted Soul Sand in the middle, made with one, two or three Nether Stars, summons a stronger Wither: Armored, Summoner or Ultimate. The Ultimate Wither can only be summoned in the Nether.

It heals over time and from the mobs it kills, fires bursts of skulls when hit, and charges at you once it's below half health or when it can't see you. It explodes when it dies, so get away.

The Armored Wither is covered in armor, the Summoner calls Wither Minions, some with Bows, and heals much faster, and the Ultimate does all of this and hits harder. Their explosions break even blocks that resist the normal Wither.
fieldguide.minecraft.allay.description: Found in the cages of Pillager Outposts, in Woodland Mansions and in Adventure Dungeons.
fieldguide.minecraft.armadillo.descripti:
Lives in Badlands. It can't be brushed: collect the Scutes it sheds now and then, which drop as a block you can place and stack.

Search #armadillo_food in EMI to see what it eats.

It can't be bred by hand: adults fall in love on their own now and then, much more often for a while after you feed them, and less in crowded areas. Breeding can fail and sometimes gives twins.
fieldguide.minecraft.axolotl.description:
Lives in Lush Caves, and a few are kept in Woodland Mansions.

Search #axolotl_food in EMI to see what it eats.

It can't be bred by hand: adults fall in love on their own now and then, much more often for a while after you feed them, and less in crowded areas. Breeding can fail and sometimes gives twins.
fieldguide.minecraft.bat.description: Lives in caves almost everywhere in the Overworld. Also flies out of Urns broken in caves.
fieldguide.minecraft.bee.description:
Comes from Bee Nests on trees in Plains, Meadows, Flower and Birch Forests and Cherry Groves, and from Beehives. Bees stay near their hive.

Search #bee_food in EMI to see what it eats.

Breeding can fail and sometimes gives twins.

Its life is very short: it grows old and dies of old age. Feeding it a Poisonous Potato stops its aging.
fieldguide.minecraft.camel.description:
Lives in Deserts. A Chest can be put on it.

Search #camel_food in EMI to see what it eats.

It can't be bred by hand: adults fall in love on their own now and then, much more often for a while after you feed them, and less in crowded areas. Breeding can fail and sometimes gives twins.
fieldguide.minecraft.cat.description:
Tame an Ocelot to get one: it turns into a Cat. A black Cat also lives in Swamp Huts. Cats slowly heal over time.

Search #cat_food in EMI to see what it eats.

It can't be bred by hand: adults fall in love on their own now and then, much more often for a while after you feed them, and less in crowded areas. Breeding can fail and sometimes gives twins.
fieldguide.minecraft.chicken.description:
Lives in plains, forests, taigas and jungles, but not in savannas or swamps. It lays eggs.

Only Melon, Pumpkin and Torchflower Seeds feed and breed it: other seeds just make it follow you. Right-click one with an empty hand to carry it on your head: it slows your falls, but also your walking.

Breeding can fail and sometimes gives twins.

Its life is short: it grows old and dies of old age. Feeding it a Poisonous Potato stops its aging.
fieldguide.minecraft.cod.description: Lives in temperate and cold oceans. Comes in random sizes.
fieldguide.minecraft.cow.description:
Lives in plains, forests, taigas and jungles, but not in savannas or swamps. It can only be milked once in a while.

Search #cow_food in EMI to see what it eats.

It can't be bred by hand: adults fall in love on their own now and then, much more often for a while after you feed them, and less in crowded areas. Breeding can fail and sometimes gives twins.

Its life is long, but it grows old and dies of old age. Feeding it a Poisonous Potato stops its aging.
fieldguide.minecraft.dolphin.description: Lives in temperate and warm oceans.
fieldguide.minecraft.donkey.description:
Lives in Plains, Meadows and Savannas. Slower than a Horse and with a lower jump, but it can carry a Chest. It swims with you on its back. A tamed Donkey and a tamed Horse can have a Mule.

Search #donkey_food in EMI to see what it eats.

All of its kind have the same stats, so breeding doesn't give better ones. Once tamed, it doesn't wander far from where you dismount it.

It can't be bred by hand: adults fall in love on their own now and then, much more often for a while after you feed them, and less in crowded areas. Breeding can fail and sometimes gives twins.
fieldguide.minecraft.fox.description:
Lives in taigas, groves and many forests. It hunts Squirrels and slowly heals over time.

Search #fox_food in EMI to see what it eats.

It can't be bred by hand: adults fall in love on their own now and then, much more often for a while after you feed them, and less in crowded areas. Breeding can fail and sometimes gives twins.
fieldguide.minecraft.frog.description:
Lives in Swamps and Mangrove Swamps. A Frog that eats a Dragonfly drops Froglass of the Dragonfly's color.

Search #frog_food in EMI to see what it eats.

It can't be bred by hand: adults fall in love on their own now and then, much more often for a while after you feed them, and less in crowded areas. Breeding can fail and sometimes gives twins.
fieldguide.minecraft.glow_squid.descript: Lives in dark water almost everywhere in the Overworld, mostly in underwater caves. Comes in random sizes.
fieldguide.minecraft.goat.description:
Lives on snowy slopes and peaks. It can only be milked once in a while.

Search #goat_food in EMI to see what it eats.

It can't be bred by hand: adults fall in love on their own now and then, much more often for a while after you feed them, and less in crowded areas. Breeding can fail and sometimes gives twins.
fieldguide.minecraft.horse.description:
Lives in Plains and Savannas. It steps up two blocks without jumping, swims with you on its back and can carry two players.

Search #minecraft:horse_food in EMI to see what it eats.

All of its kind have the same stats, so breeding doesn't give better ones. Once tamed, it doesn't wander far from where you dismount it.

It can't be bred by hand: adults fall in love on their own now and then, much more often for a while after you feed them, and less in crowded areas. Breeding can fail and sometimes gives twins.

Its life is very long, but it grows old and dies of old age. Feeding it a Poisonous Potato stops its aging.
fieldguide.minecraft.iron_golem.descript:
Build one with four Iron Blocks and a Carved Pumpkin, and Villagers living together call one now and then, more often when in danger. Some are caged in Pillager Outposts or stand guard in Woodland Mansions and Strongholds.

It's very tough. It goes back to where it was made, and Villager smiths repair it. Some monsters attack it on sight.
fieldguide.minecraft.llama.description:
Lives in Savanna Plateaus and Windswept Hills. Some Llamas carry more than others.

Search #llama_food in EMI to see what it eats.
